title: Your Cash Is Quietly Shrinking
tts: TTS unavailable (ClientConnectorDNSError: Cannot connect to host speech.platform.bing.com:443 ssl:<ssl.SSLContext object at 0x7f6f84) -> silent render + narration files for CapCut

lines.text: Hide ten thousand dollars in a drawer and it quietly loses almost half its value.
lines.visual: kinetic: Hide *$10,000* | in a drawer | and it quietly *shrinks*

lines.text: The thief is inflation. It works like compound interest in reverse.
lines.visual: stat: label=Illustrative inflation rate | value=3% | sub=of your buying power, gone every year | trend=down

lines.text: At three percent a year, that cash slides to about fifty five hundred dollars in twenty years.
lines.visual: line: title=Buying power of $10,000 at 3% inflation | x=Today,5 yrs,10 yrs,15 yrs,20 yrs | y=10000,9709,9426,9151,8885,8626,8375,8131,7894,7664,7441,7224,7014,6810,6611,6419,6232,6050,5874,5703,5537 | prefix=$ | color=bad | delta=-45% | note=Illustrative example. Not financial advice.

lines.text: So make it earn more than inflation, like a savings account paying four percent
In twenty years, it grows to about twenty one thousand nine hundred dollars
lines.visual: bar: title=Balance after 20 years | x=Drawer,Savings at 4% | y=10000,21900 | prefix=$ | highlight=1 | note=Illustrative example. Not financial advice.

lines.text: After inflation, it still buys about twelve thousand dollars Double the drawer.
lines.visual: bar: title=Buying power in today's dollars | x=Drawer,Savings at 4% | y=5500,12100 | prefix=$ | bad=0 | highlight=1

lines.text: Real return is your interest rate minus inflation.
Follow for more simple money explainers.
